project.title: Language and Algorithmic Enforcement in Public Goods Games
project.subtitle: Complete policy pilots, controlled reference mechanisms, and a versioned history of diagnostics

studies.title: Fresh complete H versus HL policy comparison
studies.version: fresh randomized complete-policy pilot; original family
studies.design: Six randomized blocks; one fresh empty-history 15-round game per arm in each block.
studies.sample: Six blocks, 12 games, 720 contributions and 2160 model returns.
studies.summary: The complete public language-policy package reduced group earnings in this fixed pilot.
findings: All six HL-H block differences were negative; mean difference -367 group tokens.
Mean H payoff 1727.4 versus HL 1360.4. Actual sanction deductions were zero.
Contribution differences appeared during the first three forced-OFF rounds.
limits: This estimates the total announced policy package, not the isolated effect of an extra ON decision or a semantic-information treatment.
Six blocks and one model/scorer remain a pilot; old one-per-arm data were not pooled.

primary_result.label: Mean HL - H net group payoff
primary_result.detail: Six fresh randomized blocks; all six differences negative.

studies.public_data_status: sanitized aggregate; original local files are provenance references, not raw API releases

studies.title: Reference inheritance and regenerated behavior
studies.version: controlled reference inheritance; original threshold
studies.design: Four producer pairs generate different donor references; recipients receive comparable candidate texts with the active reference varied and regenerate behavior.
studies.sample: Four independent producer-pair blocks; 1056 saved model returns.
studies.summary: Controlled donor-reference differences changed branch-weighted payoffs.
findings: Mean equal-weight inherited-reference contrast was -7.296 group tokens.
Recipient-policy by donor-reference interaction was exactly zero in the saved sample.
limits: Controlled checkpoint contrast, not mediation of the complete H/HL policy effect.
Single model, one source history, one fixed scorer; no general irreversible collapse or exhausted feasible trigger claim.

primary_result.label: Controlled inherited-reference contrast
primary_result.detail: Four independent producer-pair blocks; distinct from complete-policy mediation.

studies.title: Enforcement demand through a monitored language channel
studies.version: five-condition fixed sample
studies.design: Two source histories times two repeats times five LIVE/YOKED/DIRECT value conditions.
studies.sample: Four source-repeat blocks; 20 groups and 80 first-stage messages.
studies.summary: Control incentives changed expression, with source-dependent score effects.
findings: The direct button requested ON for all 16 player reports.
Within-source score interactions had opposite signs: D02 +1.1235 and P02 -1.1758.
limits: Two histories differ in disclosure and prior messages; source differences are not a clean disclosure effect.
A button can implement the request and guaranteed ON is not worse; this does not prove free language superiority or optimal adaptive sanctions.

primary_result.label: Fixed five-condition sample
primary_result.detail: Two source histories; effects remain source dependent.

studies.title: GPT/Qwen same-state punishment screen
studies.version: original payoff rule; common round-4 state
studies.design: Pure GPT, pure Qwen and mixed two-plus-two groups, two repeats, each paired ON/OFF at one common state.
studies.sample: One public history; six paired comparisons and 12 arms.
studies.summary: Every observed current-round ON-OFF payoff difference was positive.
findings: Observed pair gains ranged from 9.6 to 19.2 group tokens.
Different behavior did not create positive-versus-negative sanction values in this screen.
limits: Current round only, one shared history; six pairs are not six independent histories.
No additional language information or selective institution value was measured.

studies.title: Free out-of-fold early-warning audit
studies.version: post-run fixed feature audit; no new behavior
studies.design: Fixed local features with leave-one-game-out prediction and trajectory-family sensitivity checks on the six H games.
studies.sample: Six games; 72 eligible transitions, 69 with added-activation scope.
studies.summary: The fixed text method did not stably improve the operational prediction baselines.
findings: Candidate-set equal-game Brier: H .03433, numerical mentions .03774, raw-text additions .03854, lookup .03309.

limits: Exploratory reuse of already viewed trajectories, with post-fit feature-description clarifications retained.

studies.title: Opaque-threshold proposal: withdrawn information claim
studies.version: shelved after information-partition and transport audit
studies.design: Proposed hidden-rule chat/no-chat comparison, audited before native collection.
studies.sample: Mathematical and software checks only; no native games.

limits: This rules out a specific threshold-information argument, not every learning or coordination benefit of language.
The archived execution code had replay/persistence defects; its software fixture is not usable research evidence.

corrections.statement: Withdraw the claim that aggregating private deductions necessarily adds threshold information under the known original scalar-threshold penalty family.
A positive same-state ON-OFF difference does not imply a beneficial complete language policy.
The fresh H/HL difference includes the announced rule and behavioral adaptation before sanctions can be active; it is not an isolated extra-ON effect.
The old recipient-policy by inherited-reference interaction is zero. The proposed prospective control-by-update-policy interaction has not been measured.
Reference-sensitive scores do not establish an empty trigger set, irreversible collapse, private overmanipulation or a social-externality theorem.
Responses, messages, branches and repeated actions are not independent experimental groups. Recovered copies and shared prefixes are never new observations.
Accurate numerical reports or coded dialogue summaries in a pilot do not prove universal sufficiency of every structured communication protocol.
Mixed-model screening revealed positive ON effects at one history; it does not establish negative effects elsewhere or language information value.
Free out-of-fold forecast analysis cannot supply unobserved ON counterfactual actions or convert prediction error into welfare gains.
